deepdive.sec: Indian Alcoholic Beverages / Premiumisation & Luxury Spirits

bull_bear.body: Priority 1: Deleveraging (target net-zero debt by H1FY27). Priority 2: Dividends (minimum 20% payout policy announced). Priority 3: Organic growth capex. Inorganic M&A ruled out currently unless ROCE >20-25%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory policy changes (Karnataka pricing rationalization pending, Maharashtra MML stabilization, West Bengal govt change, Bihar prohibition status); Input cost volatility (glass, global crude/West Asia); Competition in MML segment in Maharashtra.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'inflection point', 'value-led growth', and 'financial prudence'. Clear focus on premiumisation as a structural margin driver rather than cyclical.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 90% of power/fuel at key plants (Sitapur, Rampur) is biofuel-driven, insulating against LPG crises. The company controls raw material procurement even for outsourced bottling units, mitigating supply chain hiccups. Magic Moments vodka volume (8.6mn cases) now rivals large global vodka brands in India, signaling a structural shift to white spirits among GenZ.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging is explicit and near complete: total debt of ₹212.2 Crore against ₹106.1 Crore cash, with net debt down ₹138 Crore since March 2026 and management guiding to net-debt-free by Q2 FY2027.
- Term loans have been steadily retired — down ₹57.9 Crore since March 2026 to ₹72.1 Crore — and interest cost is falling year on year.
- Marketing spend is treated as a governed allocation rather than a residual: A&SP is deliberately maintained at 6–8% of IMFL revenues across quarters to sustain growth and market share.
- Management repeatedly invokes a "disciplined approach to capital allocation" alongside improving return ratios (ROCE) as the framework tying premiumisation to shareholder value.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Luxury: INR 475cr sales value, targeting 25% growth FY27 (Brands: Rampur 1943 Virasat, Spirit of Kashmyr, Jaisalmer). Prestige & Above: Vol +28% in Q4, +20% guided for FY27 (Brands: Royal Ranthambore +50%, Magic Moments +21% vol to 8.6mn cases, After Dark +60%). Regular: Vol degrowth in Q4 due to base effects/policy, but full year +30%; guided +3-5% vol FY27. Non-IMFL: Growing 7-8%, margin ~9% vs IMFL ~20-21%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Glass bottle inflation (~15%) and potential West Asia supply chain disruptions impacting input costs for the broader alcoholic beverage sector. | Radico Khaitan Ltd | beneficiary | High | 90% biofuel dependency for power insulates from energy shocks; long-term glass contracts and pricing power via premium mix allow passing on costs, unlike smaller peers. |
| Maharashtra MML market contraction (-20-25%) and regulatory uncertainty creating volume pressure for pure-play IMFL companies without MML exposure. | Radico Khaitan Ltd | beneficiary | Med | JV with Diageo (Radico NV) provides immediate access to MML segment with target 10% market share, diversifying risk compared to competitors solely dependent on IMFL in MH. |
| Rising excise duties and lack of pricing power in the regular segment squeezing margins for mass-market alcohol producers. | Competitors focused on Regular Segment | loser | Med | Radico's regular segment volume degrowth in Q4 highlights sector weakness, but their pivot to Prestige/Luxury (28% vol growth) offsets this, whereas peers heavily weighted to regular IMFL face margin compression without the mix buffer. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Presented as one of India's leading homegrown spirits companies, with brand building, enduring consumer recall and loyalty framed as the core moat in an IMFL industry benefiting from premiumisation, favourable demographics, rising incomes and progressive state regulatory reform.
- Clear category leadership in vodka: Magic Moments holds roughly 60% of the overall Indian vodka market, positioning the company to capture the category's structural expansion (vodka saliency rose from 4.6% to 6.1% of IMFL in a year).
- Luxury credentials are built on international recognition rather than price alone — Rampur Single Malt, Rampur Asava and Jaisalmer Gin carry repeat Gold/Double Gold medals at global spirits competitions and Rampur features in Drinks International's World's 50 Most Admired Whiskies.
- Jaisalmer commands roughly 50% market share of India's luxury gin space, and Rampur is described as the most expensive Indian whisky at the entry-level scotch price point, priced above competition.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [State policy risk] Regular-segment volumes fell on a high base created by the change in route-to-market in Andhra Pradesh and policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka — a reminder that state excise regimes materially swing the mass portfolio.
- [Macro/supply chain] Management flags geopolitical uncertainty, the West Asia crisis and supply-chain disruption as live risks to input costs, requiring agility and prudent risk management.
- [Guidance] Full-year FY2027 guidance given for both P&A volume growth (over 25%) and EBITDA margin (around 20%).
- [Category shift] Vodka's share of the Indian IMFL market rose from 4.6% to 6.1% year on year, described as one of the most significant structural shifts underway in the industry.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin 48% (+450bps YoY); EBITDA 19% (+565bps YoY). Drivers: Portfolio mix, operating leverage, price hikes (~60bps benefit). Risks: Glass prices up ~15% recently (factored in); Geopolitical tension in West Asia impacting supply chain; LPG dependency minimal (90% biofuel captive power).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Luxury portfolio +25% value growth in FY27; Prestige & Above volume +20% in FY27; Regular segment volume +3-5%; Margin: EBITDA margin expansion of 125bps in FY27 (inclusive of UK-India FTA benefits and cost pushes); Capex: INR 150-175cr focused on maintenance, efficiency, and optimization.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A for FMCG; Demand signals indicate strong traction in Luxury (INR 475cr sales value) and Prestige segments with 28% vol growth in P&A in Q4.

outlook.body: On-trade expansion (1,000 advocacy sessions planned); Geographic widening of luxury brands (from 10 to 20 states); Flavor innovations in Magic Moments (Flavours of India); Export market penetration (targeting 100 airports); Potential prohibition uplift in Bihar (wait-and-watch).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Radico Khaitan delivered a milestone Q4FY26 with record 19% EBITDA margins driven by a richer portfolio mix and operating leverage, crossing INR 6,000cr revenue and INR 1,000cr EBITDA. The company is pivoting to a debt-free balance sheet by H1FY27 while guiding for 125bps margin expansion in FY27, underpinned by 20% volume growth in the Prestige & Above segment and aggressive luxury brand distribution.

open.item: Super-premium and luxury portfolio revenue is expected to be close to Rs 500 crores for FY26 versus Rs 340 crores last year.
Radico will launch Maharashtra Made Liquor (MML) through its RNV joint venture and be in the market from January 2026 onwards.
open.promised: MML launch via RNV JV text

open.item: Telangana collection issues have persisted for two years; management expects the entire old outstanding to be cleared within a month.
Management expects ENA and grain prices to stay stable to favorable in the near term, providing continued margin support, while remaining mindful of external volatility.
open.promised: stable to benign RM prices text

open.item: After Dark whisky, which sold 1.9 million cases last year, is on track to double volumes in FY26 to roughly 3.8 million cases.
open.promised: double 1.9 mn cases (~3.8 mn cases) mn cases

open.item: Management expects to deliver 20% plus overall IMFL volume growth in FY26 with robust contribution from the prestige and above category.
Radico is on track to cross Rs 500 crores of revenue from luxury and semi-luxury brands in FY26, up from roughly Rs 350 crores last year.
Radico estimates its FY26 scotch requirement at over Rs 250 crores in value and expects significant cost advantages from the FTA duty reduction to 75%.
Morpheus Super Premium Whisky, launched in UP, will be rolled out to 10 states in the second half of FY26, covering 70% of the segment.
open.promised: 10 states in H2FY26 count of states

open.item: After Dark, currently available in 14 states, will be taken national across 24 states in the next six months.
The Spirit of Kashmyr luxury vodka, launched in UP, will be extended to 10 states in the current fiscal year with an ambition to scale the brand globally.
Non-IMFL revenue is running at Rs 400-420 crores per quarter and is expected to grow at a single-digit rate from FY26 onwards, with country liquor growing 4-5%.
The regular category, which returned to a sharp growth trajectory from Q3 of last year, is expected to sustain that momentum in the next quarters.

Management flagged the drastic Maharashtra excise/duty change but noted the state is only 4-5% of volumes, there was no pre-buy stocking in the quarter, and no material profitability impact is expected.
Advertising and sales promotion spend will stay within the targeted range of 7% to 8% of revenue.
Management expects about 100 basis points of EBITDA margin improvement in FY26, before any benefit from duty reduction, with continuous margin improvement built into the model for 3 years.
Management is confident of surpassing Rs 500 crores of luxury and semi-luxury portfolio revenue in FY26, versus Rs 340 crores achieved in FY25 (up 32%).
Net debt (about Rs 600 crores) is to be reduced by around 35% to 40% during FY26.
Regular category volumes are back and should grow 12% to 13% in FY26.
Scotch (blended malt) imports in FY26 are projected to exceed Rs 250 crores at landed price including import duties, with any duty reduction flowing through as cost saving.
